text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT AND BARLEY SALE - Japan's Food Agency bought 80,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, 40,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat, 17,000 tonnes of Australian wheat and 20,000 tonnes of Australian barley in its weekly tender. The Australian wheat was for November shipment while the rest was for December shipment.

COTTONSEED MEAL SALE - South Korean feed mill companies bought 5,000 tonnes of Chinese cottonseed meal at $151.85 a tonne on a c and f. Sunkyong Ltd, a South Korean trading house, won the contract for delivery on Dec 30 to Inchon.

WHEAT SALE - South Korea's Dae Han Flour Mills Co Ltd said on Wednesday it had bought 12,500 tonnes of U.S. wheat from Japanese trading house Kanematsu Corp. Shipment was set for January 15-February 15 to Inchon. The type of wheat included soft white, 4,500 tonnes at $166.45, hard red winter, 5,500 tonnes at $190.15 and DNS, 2,500 tonnes at $190.70.

VEGOIL SALES - Egypt's official Holding Company for Food Industries bought on Wednesday 5,000 tonnes of crude kernel or coconut oil at $715 C+F per tonne for delivery in the first half of December. Egypt also bought 45,000 tonnes of sunflower and/or soya bean oil for $535.85 and $537.5 per tonne.

SOYBEAN TENDER - South Korea's Sam Yang Foods Co Ltd said it will buy 16,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 soybean by the end of this week. Shipment would be set for early November from the U.S. Gulf to South Korea's western port of Inchon.
WHEAT TENDER - Algeria has launched a tender for the import of 100,000 tonnes of U.S. and/or Canadian durum wheat for shipment in December, European grain traders said. The

results of the tender launched on October 7 are expected later this week. Algeria is seeking 50,000 tonnes of durum wheat for shipment in the first half of December and another 50,000 tonnes for shipment in the second half of December.

WHEAT TENDERS - The Taiwan Flour Mills Association will tender on Friday for two shipments totalling 60,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, traders said. The shipments contain Dark Northern Spring (DNS), Hard Red Winter (HRW) and White Wheat (WW) and are slated for delivery from the Pacific Northwest.

- The CCC said it is retendering for up to 35,000 tonnes U.S. No.2 or better hard red winter, soft white or soft red winter wheat for donation to Eritrea. Shipment was slated for Oct 30-Nov 25. Offers must be due by October 15.
- Sri Lanka is to seek October 18 100,000 tonnes optional-origin wheat for Nov 11-20 shipment.

WHEAT TENDER cont'd - Armenia will be seeking 21,000 tonnes optional origin wheat for up to November 20 shipment, its U.S. export agent said. The wheat would come from the European Community, Ukraine or if U.S. origin, only hard red winter no.2. The date for offers was Oct 14, Yerevan, Armenia.

- The Cyprus Grain Commission invited tenders for a combined cargo of 12,000 tonnes of U.S. or Canadian spring wheat and 6,000 tonnes of U.S. or Canadian durum wheat. The tender closes October 15 and shipment is November 15-30.
CORN TENDER - Taiwan's FGEP group passed on a tender for 54,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn due to high prices.
CORN TENDER - The Philippines will import 150,000 tonnes of U.S. yellow corn for December delivery, officials of the state National Food Authority (NFA) said.

MARKET TALK - Bulgaria, suffering a severe grain shortage, hopes to receive some 100,000-200,000 tonnes of Kazakh wheat in exchange for forgiving part of Kazakhstan's debt, Bulgaria's deputy prime minister said on Wednesday.

... India has halted wheat exports to curb rising domestic prices and augument supplies, traders and analysts said on Wednesday. Traders said there were no wheat exports since September 30 as the state-owned Agricultural and Food Products Export Development Authority had not issued export licences.

... Domestic corn buying is expected to pick up steam in Indonesia following the recent washout of deals with foreign sellers, traders said. An Indonesian trader said the washouts, amounting to about 70,000 tonnes of U.S. corn contracts, would help trigger local purchases later in the year particularly in Lampung where the harvest is proceeding.

... Russia's Roskhleboprodukt grain trade agency is seeking government approval to barter 400,000 tonnes of domestic food grain to Uzbekistan for an unspecified amount of cotton, a Roskhleboprodukt source said on Wednesday.
